learningObjective: Distinguish real benefits and non-benefits of kernel fusion for transformer building blocks.

canonicalClaims.claim: Kernel fusion reduces HBM roundtrips of intermediates and amortizes launch overhead; it does not change FLOP count and can hurt performance when register pressure causes spills or when reduction boundaries prevent good tiling.
conditions: Comparison is at fixed algorithm; only the kernel structure changes.
Register file / SMEM sized comparably between fused and un-fused variants.
nonImplications: Does not imply zero HBM traffic in the fused case; inputs and outputs still stream.
Does not imply fusion is always applied by compilers; it is a tunable decision.

misconceptions.whyWrong: Fusion increases register footprint and can cause spills; can lose to un-fused variants.
Fusion is a scheduling change; ops still execute their original arithmetic.

misconceptions.claim: Reduction-boundary fusion is trivial like pointwise fusion.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Reductions require cooperation across threads; fusion across them requires special tiling and often fails.

implementationFacts: Inductor prefers pointwise-with-pointwise fusion by default; reduction fusion requires shape compatibility.
CUTLASS epilogues handle common patterns (bias, activation, quantize) without giving up tensor-core throughput.
performanceScenarios: Fused RMSNorm+QKV or fused down+add+norm variants are common in LLM inference libraries.
